Priya Rao - upload 200 sample prompts and a 30-min synthetic traffic trace to shared bucket (due 2026-06-24)

summary: Discovery to align on p95 latency SLOs and throughput targets for a clinical summarization feature
Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for regulatory constraints and predictable tail latencies
Main goals: p95 <= 250ms for short responses (<=256 tokens), sustainable overall throughput of ~2k tokens/sec during peak bursts with spikes to 5k tokens/sec for short windows
transcript: [00:00:05] Maya: hey everybody thanks for joining, we got a packed agenda today — quick intros then we'll dive into p95 and throughput targets
[00:00:18] Samira (CTO): thanks, we ran into weird tail latency issues with our current vendor when convo length spikes, so main ask is consistent p95 across peaks
[00:00:35] Diego (SE): got it. quick q: are you already measuring p95 at token-level or response-level? different tooling there.
[00:00:46] Priya: We measure response-level from our API gateway. It's a mix — sometimes the gateway adds jitter so the raw model p95 is a bit lower. we can provide traces though.

[00:01:10] Ben: infra question — we currently have GCP with preemptible GPUs for batch jobs and a dedicated small fleet of 2xA100 for inference. thinking about whether Redwood Dedicated makes sense vs hosted with VPC peering.

[00:02:03] Diego: for p95 predictability Dedicated helps because capacity is isolated, but Hosted has smart routing and fallbacks. There's also cache and batching levers that change tokens/sec economics — prefix caching can knock down calls a lot if prompts are similar.

[00:03:12] Priya: our clinical summarizer often has shared templates so prefix cache should help, but we also have many unique patient prompts that won't cache well. So we need worst-case p95 guarantees.
[00:04:05] Maya: what's your target p95? you mentioned < 300ms before the call in email?

[00:04:14] Priya: ideally <= 250ms for short answers up to 256 tokens. For longer flows up to 1024 tokens we can accept 800-1000ms p95. Also peak concurrency target is tricky — we expect 60 concurrent user flows at peak but each flow may stream tokens back to user.
[00:04:45] Evan: to give more color, our expected steady-state is ~800 tokens/sec, bursts up to ~5k tokens/sec for 30-90s when batch ingestion runs — those bursts are what kills p95 right now.

[00:05:30] Diego: ok good. Two dimensions: steady throughput (tokens/sec) and burstability (ops/sec and concurrent streams). We use continuous batching and dynamic allocation to smooth cost while preserving tail latencies. For Dedicated you can also configure burst capacity.
[00:06:40] Ben: curious about streaming overheads — we stream token-by-token to client via websocket; what adds latency there vs non-streaming?

[00:07:05] Diego: streaming overhead is mostly at framing and network; small tokens can increase backpressure. Our runtime supports chunking and configurable flush intervals to hit p95 targets — if you need strict p95 for first token, that's a separate SLO and needs warm caches and prewarmed processes.
[00:08:12] Samira: warm vs cold start — we saw huge p99 spikes on cold workers. can Dedicated eliminate colds?

[00:08:33] Diego: Dedicated with reserved pools and warm-up policies reduces cold starts a lot. We also offer keep-alive prewarming and a minimum replica count. For private on-prem you control eviction which helps too.
[00:09:50] Priya: benchmarks — do you have a standard tokens/sec test harness we can run? we prefer to run in our environment to replicate network and gateway behavior.

[00:10:12] Maya: yes — we have a perf spreadsheet and a small harness. I'll share a link after the call. Diego can also run a Redwood-hosted baseline against a comparable model and hardware if that helps.
[00:10:40] Priya: please do both, we want Redwood's baseline and our in-house run. Also include p50/p95/p99 and token/sec as columns, and note warm vs cold run tags.
[00:11:25] Diego: noted. For modeling: which model family are you targeting? smaller finetuned Llama-like or larger 70B class?
[00:11:35] Priya: we're on a finetuned 13B for summaries today, but we plan 70B experiments later. so the PoC should focus on 13B latency profiles.
[00:12:05] Evan: on tokenization, we sometimes get large output tokens which changes tokens/sec math — small tokens vs big tokens. Can Redwood report tokenization overheads too?

[00:12:24] Diego: yes we'll include tokenization time and end-to-end breakdown: model compute, runtime overhead, network, and SDK/codec time. We'll also show how KV cache affects step-time for multi-turn dialogues.
[00:13:40] Ben: curious about the quantization and perf tradeoffs — can you recommend quantization profiles to hit our p95?

[00:14:00] Diego: we have recommended quantization limits per model that trade accuracy vs latency; for 13B often int8 or q4 might be sweet spots. Redwood Optimize can suggest profiles based on your eval set and target SLOs.

[00:15:20] Priya: security constraints: we must ensure PHI never leaves our VPC for production due to compliance — likely Private or Dedicated with VPC peering and customer KMS. Any difference in latency there?

[00:15:40] Maya: VPC peering is low latency; Dedicated in-region with VPC is typically similar to Hosted in terms of network latency. On-prem adds variability but gives strongest control. We'll include encryption/KMS notes in the security pack.
[00:16:50] Samira: procurement question — what's the minimum Reserved capacity for Dedicated? we don't want to overcommit before validation.

[00:17:10] Maya: we have small tier reserved pools starting at equivalent of 1xA100 throughput block for monthly commitment; within PoC we can provide short-term dedicated pilot pricing. I'll include numbers in the quote.
[00:18:00] Evan: can Redwood simulate our burst pattern (5k tokens/sec for 60s) on the dedicated pilot?

[00:18:20] Diego: yes, we can run synthetic traffic replays against Dedicated and measure p95 across warm and cold windows. We recommend a 30–60 minute replay that includes several bursts to capture queueing effects.
[00:19:02] Ben: what about autoscaling — does it introduce extra tail latency while scaling up?

[00:19:18] Diego: scaling can introduce brief transient friction; we mitigate with overprovisioned min replicas and burst capacity. With Dedicated you can avoid autoscale cold ramps by increasing min replicas.

[00:20:30] Priya: a practical ask — can you provide an example run where p95 stayed below 250ms at 2k tokens/sec on 13B? If you have a public benchmark that approximates that that would help the execs.
[00:20:50] Maya: we have internal benchmark blobs, will redact customer specifics and share a sanitized CSV and chart. I'll attach to the follow-up email.
[00:21:37] Samira: also interested in routing fallbacks — if Dedicated hits capacity, does Hosted fallback route and what's the risk to PHI?

[00:21:55] Diego: fallback paths can be configured; for PHI you'd typically not fallback to public hosted. Instead you can route to a quieter Dedicated pool in another region, or to a smaller model variant that stays within your control plane.
[00:22:30] Priya: for our PoC can we test both: dedicated-only and dedicated-with-quiet-fallback?
[00:22:43] Diego: yes, we can set up two policies and run back-to-back replays to compare p95 and cost.

[00:23:50] Evan: minor note — our gateway currently aggregates 50ms per request; if Redwood reports model p95 at 180ms we still may be at 230ms end-to-end, so we need joint SLOs. Will Redwood help with combining traces?
[00:24:10] Lena (CSM): we can work with you to map gateway latency + model latency and produce an end-to-end report, we'll include tracer instrumentation hints in the security pack.
[00:25:40] Priya: timeline — we'd like a pilot in the next two weeks to run with real-ish traffic before a Q3 decision.
[00:25:55] Maya: sounds good — we'll target the bench week of 2026-06-28. Action items as listed in the follow-ups. Any other blockers?
[00:26:10] Ben: maybe one — monitoring. Do you expose token-level telemetry and per-replica traces to customers?

[00:26:30] Diego: yes, Console exposes per-route latency histograms, token counts, replica-level CPU/GPU utilization. For Private we can ship prometheus metrics or provide our hosted console with RBAC.
[00:27:05] Samira: thanks, that's helpful. we'll get prompts uploaded. last q: any gotchas for streaming RN — we saw chunking causing jitter in mobile clients.
[00:27:20] Diego: mobile jitter usually due to small write buffers and TCP Nagle — we can tune chunk sizes and flush intervals; we'll surface recommended client settings in the follow-up.
[00:28:02] Maya: ok wrapping up — I'll send the perf spreadsheet, security pack, and proposed pilot quote. Diego will run baseline runs in parallel and Lena will book the PoC slot. Thanks everyone.
[00:28:20] Priya: thanks, appreciate it. looking forward to the data.
[00:28:35] Samira: bye all.
